# Field reference

Every field a filter can use. A protocol name (`tcp`) tests that the header is present,
and slices as its bytes (`tcp[13]`). The symbolic names are Avulse extensions: Wireshark's
own value labels (`ip.proto == "UDP"`) work too.

## Wireshark fields

They have the same name and meaning as in Wireshark.

### frame

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frame` | protocol | The whole packet |
| `frame.len` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | Packet length in bytes |
| `frame.cap_len` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | Captured length in bytes (same as frame.len) |
| `frame.interface_name` | string | Interface name |

### eth

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `eth` | protocol | Ethernet header (ETHERNET layer) |
| `eth.dst` | MAC address | Destination MAC |
| `eth.src` | MAC address | Source MAC |
| `eth.addr` | MAC address | Source or destination MAC |
| `eth.type` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | EtherType of the outer header. Names: `ipv4`, `ip`, `arp`, `vlan`, `ipv6`, `mpls`, `pppoe-discovery`, `pppoe-session`, `eapol`, `qinq`, `lldp` |

### vlan

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vlan` | protocol | 802.1Q tag (each tag; 802.1ad tags are `ieee8021ad`) |
| `vlan.priority` | unsigned integer (3 bits) | Priority code point |
| `vlan.dei` | boolean | Drop eligible indicator |
| `vlan.id` | unsigned integer (12 bits) | VLAN ID |
| `vlan.etype` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | EtherType after the tag. Names: `ipv4`, `ip`, `arp`, `vlan`, `ipv6`, `mpls`, `pppoe-discovery`, `pppoe-session`, `eapol`, `qinq`, `lldp` |

### ip

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ip` | protocol | IPv4 header |
| `ip.version` | unsigned integer (4 bits) | Version (of the IPv4 or the IPv6 header, as in Wireshark) |
| `ip.hdr_len` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Header length in bytes |

| `ip.flags` | unsigned integer (3 bits) | Flags (reserved, DF, MF) |

| `ip.flags.df` | boolean | Don't fragment |
| `ip.flags.mf` | boolean | More fragments |
| `ip.frag_offset` | unsigned integer (13 bits) | Fragment offset (8-byte units) |
| `ip.ttl` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Time to live |
| `ip.proto` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Protocol. Names: `hopopt`, `icmp`, `igmp`, `tcp`, `udp`, `ipv6-route`, `ipv6-frag`, `gre`, `esp`, `ah`, `icmpv6`, `ipv6-nonxt`, `ipv6-opts`, `sctp` |
| `ip.checksum` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | Header checksum |
| `ip.src` | IPv4 address | Source address |
| `ip.dst` | IPv4 address | Destination address |
| `ip.addr` | IPv4 address | Source or destination address |

## Avulse extensions

Metadata that is not in the packet bytes. Bare, the flags (`outbound`, `loopback`, …) test
that the value is true.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inbound` | boolean | Inbound packet |
| `outbound` | boolean | Outbound packet |
| `loopback` | boolean | Loopback packet |
| `impostor` | boolean | Packet injected by another handle |
| `fragment` | boolean | IP fragment |
| `ifidx` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | Interface index |
| `subifidx` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | Sub-interface index |
| `iface` | string | Interface name |
| `layer` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Layer of the handle. Names: `network`, `network-forward`, `flow`, `socket`, `reflect`, `ethernet` |
| `event` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Event. Names: `packet`, `established`, `deleted`, `bind`, `connect`, `listen`, `accept`, `close`, `open`, `reflect-open`, `reflect-close` |
| `protocol` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | Transport protocol (after IPv6 extension headers). Names: `hopopt`, `icmp`, `igmp`, `tcp`, `udp`, `ipv6-route`, `ipv6-frag`, `gre`, `esp`, `ah`, `icmpv6`, `ipv6-nonxt`, `ipv6-opts`, `sctp` |
| `local.addr` | IP address | Local address |
| `remote.addr` | IP address | Remote address |
| `local.port` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | Local port |
| `remote.port` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | Remote port |
| `process.pid` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | Process ID (FLOW, SOCKET layers) |
| `process.name` | string | Process name (FLOW, SOCKET layers) |
| `endpoint.id` | unsigned integer (64 bits) | Endpoint ID (FLOW, SOCKET layers) |
| `parent.endpoint.id` | unsigned integer (64 bits) | Parent endpoint ID (FLOW, SOCKET layers) |
| `timestamp` | integer | Timestamp of the packet or event, as the backend reports it |
| `priority` | integer | Priority of the handle (REFLECT layer: of the handle the event is about) |
| `random8` | unsigned integer (8 bits) | 8 bits of a per-packet hash (WinDivert's `random8`) |
| `random16` | unsigned integer (16 bits) | 16 bits of a per-packet hash (WinDivert's `random16`) |
| `random32` | unsigned integer (32 bits) | 32 bits of a per-packet hash (WinDivert's `random32`) |

## Rejected Wireshark fields

These need state across packets or name resolution, so a filter that uses them is an
error with this hint.

| Field | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `tcp.seq` | relative sequence numbers need stream tracking; use `tcp.seq_raw` |
| `tcp.ack` | relative acknowledgment numbers need stream tracking; use `tcp.ack_raw` |
| `tcp.nxtseq` | needs stream tracking |
| `tcp.window_size` | the scaled window needs the handshake; use `tcp.window_size_value` |
| `tcp.window_size_scalefactor` | needs the handshake |
| `tcp.stream` | stream indexes need connection tracking |
| `udp.stream` | stream indexes need connection tracking |
| `tcp.analysis` | TCP analysis needs stream tracking |
| `tcp.time_delta` | needs stream tracking |
| `tcp.time_relative` | needs stream tracking |
| `tcp.segment` | needs TCP reassembly |
| `tcp.reassembled` | needs TCP reassembly |
| `tcp.option_kind` | a header has up to 40 options, more than a field can hold; test an option, e.g. `tcp.options.sack_perm`, or search `tcp.options` |
| `tcp.option_len` | a header has up to 40 options, more than a field can hold; test an option, e.g. `tcp.options.sack_perm`, or search `tcp.options` |
| `tcp.options.nop` | NOP options repeat; search the option bytes, e.g. `tcp.options contains 01:01` |
| `tcp.options.eol` | search the option bytes, e.g. `tcp.options contains 00` |
| `tcp.options.sack` | SACK edges are relative sequence numbers, which need stream tracking |
| `tcp.options.sack_le` | SACK edges are relative sequence numbers, which need stream tracking |
| `tcp.options.sack_re` | SACK edges are relative sequence numbers, which need stream tracking |
| `tcp.options` | this TCP option is not decoded; slice `tcp.options` instead, e.g. `tcp.options[0] == 02` |
| `ip.host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `ip.src_host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `ip.dst_host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `ipv6.host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `ipv6.src_host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `ipv6.dst_host` | host names need DNS; compare addresses |
| `eth.src_resolved` | vendor names are not resolved; compare addresses |
| `eth.dst_resolved` | vendor names are not resolved; compare addresses |
| `frame.time` | timestamps are not filterable |
| `frame.number` | packet numbers are not filterable |
| `frame.protocols` | use the protocol names directly, e.g. `tcp` |

Protocols that Avulse does not decode are rejected too: `http`, `http2`, `http3`, `tls`, `ssl`, `dtls`, `dns`, `mdns`, `llmnr`, `nbns`, `quic`, `dhcp`, `bootp`, `dhcpv6`, `ssh`, `smb`, `smb2`, `ftp`, `ftp-data`, `smtp`, `imap`, `pop`, `ntp`, `snmp`, `sip`, `rtp`, `rtcp`, `kerberos`, `ldap`, `ssdp`, `websocket`, `mqtt`, `grpc`, `telnet`, `rdp`, `nfs`, `data`, `igmp`, `gre`, `sctp`, `esp`, `ah`, `stp`, `cdp`, `lldp`, `eapol`, `pppoe`, `mpls`, `vxlan`, `geneve`. Match their bytes instead, such as `udp.port == 53` or
`tcp.payload contains "HTTP/1.1"`.
